615.unvetted: Unopened editions that would cover the unread part: Antonio de la Torre, Documentos sobre relaciones internacionales de los Reyes Catolicos vol. V (1495-1497, CSIC 1965), and Suarez Fernandez, Politica internacional de Isabel la Catolica vol. IV (1972). Neither is on archive.org (advancedsearch 0 hits); Google Books gives the set no preview or snippet only, and searches there for the despatch returned nothing either way. Either may print the clear draft of 28 Dec 1495 in full, so the prior-art question is unanswered. Opened: CSP Spain I pp. 72-79 (BHO in Chrome): no. 113 is an English abstract of the draft with quotations, no. 114 notices the cipher copy ('Written in two different keys of cipher, one of which is extant') with no decipherment. Tomokiyo, spanish.htm: lists PTR 52 doc. 124 as 'another undated letter' in a list of letters probably using the code, with no reading. Not checked: Rymer, Rodriguez Villa, Mattingly (no text opened; none is known to print this despatch). New for whoever resumes: CSP no. 117 (pp. 75-77), the merchant-cover letter of the same day from 'MCCCIX (Guide)' to Alonzo de Compludo, also names Diego de Soria, Juan de Santa Gadea and the Company, and Bergenroth prints its groups deciphered. Doc. 124 uses the same cover words, so compare doc. 124 with no. 117 as well as no. 113: the identification with no. 113 alone is not settled. If de la Torre V and Suarez IV show no print, the block can be open with key_held AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33.

864.evidence: Warburton III pp. 125-128 prints Digby to Legge, undated, with Legge's reply placing it at Hereford, 30 June 1645: continuous plain English, no gap and no cipher mark, though Warburton marks cipher elsewhere (p. 153). Quote: 'Prince Rupert is neither gainable nor tenable by me'. It covers the explanations of defeat, but not the 'Proposals on which a meeting between King and Parliament might be arranged' in the Staffordshire description. BL Add MS 18982 ff. 66r-67v is a copy, 'Partially in cipher (deciphered)' (BL catalogue; leaf not seen, IIIF 403). Legge mentions a duplicate.
864.closed: The letter is in print and a deciphered copy is at BL, so the 'coded part' is very likely read, but which passage is coded in /56 cannot be told without the leaf, and the proposals are not in Warburton.

865.evidence: Warburton III has no letter of 9 Aug 1645. Rupert's letters stop at 'Bristol, July 29, 1645' (p. 155), then Digby's of Aug. 27 and 29 and Bristol siege papers; a text search for 9 August finds only Paris 1653. BL Add MS 18982 lists nothing of that date. HMC Dartmouth I and III have no 1645 text. So no decipherment found; the letter is still not seen.
